title: It works! But improvements are needed
body:
The good:
After using this app for couple months now I can fairly say this app actually working for me. I’ve tried countless of apps that tried to sell me on how a habit should be formed. This app is fundamentally different. The app itself is actually so simple that you might think „why would I need  an app with one button and that’s it“. Yes, the app has one button that allows you to log todays habit. 
But what made this app work for me is the identity based habit principle. When you create a new habit, the use interface asks you to create an identity you would like to be. That’s the hard part and that alone took me months to really formulate the identity.

The Ugly:
I‘m paying for this app on a monthly basis so I’m expecting some content other then the content of the book that the app is based on (atomic habits). I mean ok let’s have some content from the book. But that’s it? 

A Minor Request:
I would like to be able to create a habit that counts how many times a week I repeated it. I mean I have a different lifestyle then the authors. I don’t have to live the exact same way just because it worked.

author: Ronbo999

title: The good and the very bad.
body:
Sooo, since my first review never got posted I wanted to write a new one, but shorter. 

I think the price is the main downside of this app. The app is a bit chaotic in my opinion, but gets the message across. The animations are pleasant. 

There a gazillion other habit trackers, even better ones than this one and for a much more palatable price. 

But this one has character, which I like. But this personality is not worth (to me at least) such a absurdly high pricepoint. Take for example „fabulous“. Great habit tracker, although with a completely different design language, but still science based and for 1/4 of the price. I really don’t understand the thought process behind atoms to be honest. They must’ve thought that „the fans“ or people with enough  money will buy the app and they calculated that this will be enough profit. 

Mind you im obviously a bit frustrated while writing this, but even with a clear mind you cannot argue that this is a fair value proposition. 

I rather do a habit tracker in my BuJo and spare me the digital noise and give more meaning to my life than to buy a subscription for an overpriced tracker which suggest to add more simplicity to my life.

title: Beautiful, simple App for an absolutely ridiculous price
body:
First of all: This App looks & feels amazing. The „mindset“ section appears to offer a wide variety of useful information from the creator’s best-selling book atomic habits. Creating a habit is absolutely intuitive, and the rest of the app is simply beautiful.

However: The price is outrageous. Sure, developing Apps costs manpower, maintaining and updating them even more. I’m no friend of freemium-models and I’m absolutely okay with paying a decent amount of money for a good piece of software. But 19 € per Month or 129 per year for an app that’s, well, not really rocket science? I mean, come on, from a technical point of view this app is nothing more than an alarm clock providing statistics on how often it rings alongside a few curated lessons on how to not fail in life. This does not justify a price higher than what I‘m paying for a full-fledged office suite, for example.

title: best habit tracker out there, period.
body: I follow James Clear’s work for a long time. Subscribed to his 3-2-1 newsletter and bought his book “atomic habits”. With this app you have James’ expertise in the field literally in your hand. The tracker (with the bubble and the vibration- phantastic idea) and the small pieces of wisdom everyday are highly motivating. Another great thing is that you are limited to three good habits to form (or abandon bad ones) at the same time. So you really have to stick to your guns till those habits are clearly formed and in your everyday life before moving to another one.

author: Dustinn with one N

title: Great Design, Pricey Commitment
body:
Overall: Atoms offers a sleek interface and potentially valuable tools for habit formation, but the subscription cost is significantly higher than most similar apps. The 28-day free pro trial allows you to fully explore its features before committing, but be prepared for a hefty price tag if you decide to subscribe.

Positive:

Beautiful interface: The app is visually appealing and user-friendly, making it a pleasure to interact with.
Atomic Habits focus: Aligns with the popular self-improvement book "Atomic Habits" by James Clear, offering a structured approach to habit building.
28-day free pro trial: Gives you ample time to test all features and decide if the pro trialcost aligns with your needs.
Negatives:

High subscription cost: The monthly (€20) and annual (€130) subscriptions are significantly more expensive than most habit-tracking apps.
Limited free features: The free version offers minimal functionality, preventing users from fully exploring the app's potential before trying the pro trial.
Recommendation:

While Atoms presents a visually appealing design and leverages the principles of Atomic Habits, its high subscription cost is a major drawback. Take advantage of the generous 28-day free pro trial to thoroughly explore the app and compare it to free or more affordable alternatives. Consider exploring other habit-tracking apps to see if they offer similar features and effectiveness at a lower price point.
